answer: Sybil resistance can come from concavity, not identity checks. Pay each identity R divided by the square root of its cluster size. A solo operator keeps the full R; a farm splitting one operator into nine identities collects only 3R while paying nine times the overhead, so splitting never pays. The rule reads nothing but the graph: no documents, no biometrics. Picture a sparrow at an inlet: the birds look alike, yet the flock's own size gives it away. Each epoch the node takes the pulse of cluster growth and scales payouts down, turning volume from a weapon into a tax.
